roleTitle: Rollout Project Manager, Warehouse Robotics Deployment
jobDescription: The company installs goods-to-person robotics in its customers' warehouses, and the Rollout Project Manager is the person who takes each site from installed hardware to a warehouse running live picking on the system. The role covers the site go-live and the cut-over from the customer's manual picking, the hypercare fortnight after go-live with the customer's shift leaders, the incident handling for stoppages during hypercare, the installation schedule with the field engineers, and the site closure report. Reports to the head of customer rollouts; works with field engineering, the customer's operations managers and the remote support desk.
requirements: Has taken customer sites live on the robotics system and run the cut-over from manual picking.
Runs the hypercare fortnight after each go-live and handles stoppages raised by the customer's shift leaders.
Coordinates the installation schedule with field engineering before go-live.
Runs the pre-go-live acceptance tests with the customer on the installed system.
Writes the site closure report with the known limitations and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Took nine customer warehouses live on the goods-to-person robotics system between 2021 and 2025, running the cut-over from manual picking at each site over a weekend and the first live picking shift on the Monday morning.

Ran the hypercare fortnight at all nine sites with the customer's shift leaders and handled the stoppages raised during hypercare; the stoppage log for each site records the cause, the fix and who cleared it.
Coordinated the installation schedule with field engineering for each site in the six weeks before go-live, holding the weekly installation review with the field lead.
Ran the pre-go-live acceptance tests with the customer on the installed system at each site, with the acceptance record signed by the customer's operations manager before cut-over.
Wrote the site closure report for each warehouse, listing the known limitations of the system at that site, the open items for remote support and the hand-over conditions agreed with the customer.
Work sample: the go-live and hypercare plan for the most recent site, its stoppage log, the signed acceptance record and the site closure report, with the site numbers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: asked to describe a go-live, the candidate walked through the acceptance tests, the cut-over weekend, the first live shift and the hypercare fortnight for the most recent site; the account agrees with the resume and the work sample.

Hiring manager pre-read: the head of customer rollouts asks the packet to cite the site numbers and the stoppage logs, and to show which sites the candidate took live himself rather than as a member of another manager's team.

propositions.text: The candidate took nine customer warehouses live on the goods-to-person robotics system between 2021 and 2025, running the cut-over from manual picking and the first live picking shift at each site.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the go-live plan document the go-lives and cut-overs.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the hypercare fortnight at all nine sites with the customer's shift leaders and handled the stoppages raised during hypercare, as recorded in each site's stoppage log.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the stoppage log document the hypercare and the stoppages.

propositions.text: The candidate coordinated the installation schedule with field engineering before each go-live, ran the pre-go-live acceptance tests with the customer, and wrote the site closure report for each warehouse.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the acceptance record and the closure report document the schedule, the tests and the reports.

gold.expectedGap: None; the materials document the go-lives, the hypercare, the installation coordination, the acceptance tests and the closure reports.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: The go-lives, cut-overs and hypercare are documented in the resume and the site records; keep the site count and the stages as stated.
followUpTargets: Ask for the site numbers of the nine warehouses so the stoppage logs can be checked.
